subject: Agriculture
title: Water Footprint of Food
description: Learn Water Footprint of Food in one minute.

hook.text: One kilogram of almonds requires 16,000 liters of water. One kilogram of beef needs 15,000. Both are water hogs.

buildup.text: Agriculture uses 70% of all freshwater withdrawals globally. What we eat determines how much water we use.

discovery.text: Virtual water trade—water embedded in exported food—means dry countries import water as crops.

twist.text: Growing water-intensive crops in deserts with irrigation—like alfalfa in Saudi Arabia—depletes fossil aquifers permanently.

climax.text: Shifting diets toward less water-intensive foods could reduce agricultural water use by 20–30%.

punchline.text: Every bite of food is a glass of invisible water. Diet is water policy.

quiz.question: What percentage of global freshwater withdrawals goes to agriculture?
